scope.existingUniverse: All ideas in data/ideas.json re-screened; no base-conviction changes without new stock-specific evidence.

macro.summary: Sunday risk setup is less friendly to long-duration/speculative equities: US futures opened slightly lower after hawkish Jackson Hole repricing, while oil rebounded on renewed Hormuz tension. The physical AI/power thesis remains intact, but financing and valuation discipline remain essential.
macro.oil: WTI/Brent rebounded roughly 2.5% in Sunday trading on renewed Hormuz tension. Keep crude geopolitical risk separate from the more persistent refined-product bottleneck thesis.
macro.aiFinancing: Alibaba's roughly $10B Hong Kong equity raise to fund AI capex is further evidence that AI demand can remain strong while financing/dilution and ROIC become first-class risks.
macro.malaysiaDataCentres: Singapore's constrained new capacity continues to redirect incremental data-centre demand toward Johor; this reinforces grid, cable, substation and reliable-power exposure rather than adding another generic data-centre developer.

powerGrid.evidence: Malaysia's grid/substation chain received another hard earnings confirmation: MN Holdings FY26 revenue rose 61% to RM869.19M and PAT rose 92% to RM92.47M, led by substation engineering. US secure-grid policy remains supportive for domestic/approved equipment suppliers.
powerGrid.implication: Maintain preference for GEV, PWR, ETN, TNB, Southern Cable and other backlog-rich physical infrastructure. Raise MN Holdings research priority, but do not mechanically promote conviction without valuation/technical review.

aiDataCentres.evidence: Power availability and financing remain the two gating variables. Malaysia/Johor benefits from Singapore capacity constraints; Alibaba equity financing reinforces the capital-intensity/ROIC risk lens.
aiDataCentres.implication: Prefer power distribution, cooling, networking and packaging over capital-hungry developers where valuation assumes uninterrupted capex.

nuclear.evidence: No new evidence today changes the hierarchy established after Army Janus: operating nuclear, components and fuel remain preferable to pre-commercial reactor duration.
nuclear.implication: BWXT/CEG/1816.HK and fuel remain higher-quality than development-stage SMR optionality.

uraniumFuel.evidence: No new contract/supply development today cleared the bar for a conviction change.

oilGas.evidence: Sunday oil prices rebounded on renewed Hormuz tension. Dayang still has RM4.72B order-book visibility but weak H1 execution; YTL/AI gas-power crossover remains structurally relevant.
oilGas.implication: Do not confuse geopolitical crude spikes with durable upstream upgrades. Integrated/refining/logistics and gas-to-power remain differentiated expressions.

metals.evidence: Grid/data-centre copper demand remains structurally supportive, while China domestic-demand uncertainty prevents a broad cyclical upgrade.
metals.implication: Prefer bottleneck-linked copper exposure over indiscriminate China reflation beta.

roboticsAutomation.evidence: Unitree's Shanghai listing is useful commercial evidence but not a new Power Stack buy: after a 460% debut surge the shares subsequently fell about 45%, while adjusted profit had declined 53% in early 2026. The valuation episode reinforces the need to separate robot shipment/adoption evidence from equity price quality.
roboticsAutomation.implication: SYM/CGNX and commercially proven automation remain preferable to humanoid narrative exposure. Unitree is watch-only until valuation and earnings normalize.

watch.reason: First listed mainland humanoid leader with real shipments and revenue, but post-IPO valuation/speculation and falling adjusted profit fail the quality/valuation bar.

watch.name: Aggreko
watch.reason: Time-to-power exposure remains differentiated; await final IPO valuation, leverage and sponsor sell-down.

notableExistingOpportunity.name: MN Holdings
notableExistingOpportunity.evidence: FY26 revenue +61% to RM869.19M; PAT +92% to RM92.47M; substation engineering revenue RM766.46M and ~88% of group revenue.
notableExistingOpportunity.decision: No formal conviction change until current valuation/technical entry and customer/project concentration are rechecked.

currentHoldingsReview.nextTest: Sep 3 Cybercab event, measurable paid deployment economics, energy-storage margins and auto margin stabilization.

currentHoldingsReview.stockSpecificEvidence: Q2 profit -57.2% y/y and revenue -39.7%; vessel utilisation 58% versus 64%, but order book remains about RM4.72B.

currentHoldingsReview.fundamentalScoreDecision: Keep 57/C; do not average down on macro alone.
currentHoldingsReview.nextTest: Q3 work-order conversion, vessel utilisation, charter income and backlog burn.
